discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution based on the physical laws of quantum mechanics (BB84 and entanglement-based E91)

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84, 1984) showed that the quantum no-cloning principle and measurement disturbance make secret-key distribution possible with security guaranteed by physics rather than computational assumptions. Ekert (1991) linked cryptographic security directly to entanglement and violation of Bell inequalities, turning a foundational test of quantum mechanics into a working resource. This insight founded device-independent cryptography. Together these works created the field of quantum information as an experimental discipline. Single-photon sources and detectors, multiphoton entanglement, teleportation and entanglement swapping were all developed to realize their protocols. Today QKD runs over metropolitan fibre networks and satellite links, and national quantum communication infrastructures, including Sweden's, are built on it. The 2022 Prize honoured experimental tests of Bell inequalities; the conceptual discovery that quantum laws themselves guarantee secure communication is an equally fundamental and transformative contribution to physics.
